selected.concept: Retrofit X-ray computed-laminography kit for advanced-packaging failure analysis
named_buyer_examples: Guangzhou Guangxin Packaging Substrate and Wuxi Shennan Circuits X-ray inspection teams (CN)
NIST CHIPS advanced-packaging metrology programs and US packaging failure-analysis laboratories (US)
selected.painful_job: Flat multilayer substrates and advanced packages hide cracks, voids, bridges, and layer offsets behind overlapping 2D projections. Buyers already procure X-ray inspection cabinets, while high-resolution CT/XRM systems are costly, slow, and usually sold as complete cabinets.
selected.product: A tilted precision stage, cabinet-specific geometry calibration target, sparse-view reconstruction software, and package-defect classifier retrofitted to qualifying installed 2D X-ray cabinets. It does not replace the X-ray source or shielding enclosure.
selected.noncosmetic_wedge: ZEISS, Sigray, Nikon, and Nordson sell complete inspection systems. The wedge is installed-base reuse plus tilted laminography geometry for flat packages, with a two-brand calibration and repeatability dossier. A software-only classifier would be cosmetic; the stage, geometry calibration, and cabinet-compatibility qualification are the product.
selected.precompany_plan_2026_2029: 2026-2027: build the tilted-stage and calibration stack on rented or partner cabinets. 2028: blinded coupon study and two-cabinet-brand port. 2029: paid evaluation at one CN substrate/package facility and one US failure-analysis laboratory; freeze the compatibility list and service procedure.
selected.launch_2030_timing_thesis: JCET's Lingang advanced-packaging factory has phase-one production-equipment completion targeted for H2 2028, while the official 2026-2030 national plan calls for decisive integrated-circuit breakthroughs. A 2030 launch enters the post-installation yield-learning and recurring failure-analysis cycle rather than trying to win the original cabinet order.
selected.demand_trigger_2030_2034: Yield ramp, package-mix expansion, and service retrofits after 2028 advanced-packaging tool installation, plus recurring US CHIPS metrology and failure-analysis demand. Revalidate the installed 2D-cabinet population and paid retrofit appetite in 2029.
selected.competition_outlook_2030: Complete-cabinet competitors include ZEISS Versa XRM 730, Sigray Apex-class systems, Nikon XT H, and Nordson DAGE Quadra. They can add laminography modes or discount new cabinets. The thesis survives only if a retrofit produces useful 3D defect separation on at least two installed cabinet brands at a small fraction of cabinet-replacement cost.
selected.china_route: Sell a locally integrated stage, calibration artifact, and independently developed reconstruction stack to civilian semiconductor packaging and substrate plants. No controlled US source design is transferred; screen end users and exclude restricted military or surveillance uses.

first_experiment.design: Use one rented and one partner 2D X-ray cabinet to image 100 blinded flat-package or substrate coupons with seeded 10-30 micrometre void, crack, bridge, and layer-offset defects. Compare against destructive sectioning or trusted reference CT.
success_thresholds: >=90% sensitivity across the prespecified seeded-defect set
<=5 minutes per package or <=10 minutes per panel coupon
installation on two cabinet brands without source or shielding modification
kill_thresholds: Any sensitivity, false-positive, throughput, or repeatability threshold misses after the frozen calibration protocol
Porting requires cabinet-source modification or vendor-locked service access
No paid evaluation or buyer LOI after the witnessed blinded study

G1.rationale: Two independent MOFCOM buyer procurements establish active X-ray inspection purchasing, and NIST separately procures high-resolution XRM for semiconductor-package metrology.

G2.rationale: The load-bearing technical claim is supported by a final 2025 peer-reviewed Microelectronics Reliability paper; achieved startup performance is not assumed.

G3.rationale: A 12-month $92k experiment has frozen blinded-detection, speed, repeatability, compatibility, and buyer kill criteria.

G4.rationale: Exact complete-system competitors are named. Installed-cabinet retrofit is noncosmetic, but incumbents can absorb the geometry mode.

G5.rationale: Tilted laminography and sparse-view reconstruction are demonstrated; the experiment falsifies whether cabinet geometry and signal quality are sufficient.

G6.rationale: Civilian packaging plants are reachable through local integration and independent software, with end-use screening and no controlled source transfer.

G7.rationale: H2-2028 advanced-packaging equipment completion, the official 2026-2030 IC program, and continuing NIST metrology procurement support a specific 2030 post-install yield-ramp window.

selected.concept: Field-deployable industrial high-temperature heat-pump commissioning and measurement-and-verification island
named_buyer_examples: Industrial heat-pump integrators and owners responding to MIIT variable-load efficiency requirements (CN)
US ESCOs and high-temperature heat-pump field-demonstration teams (US)
selected.painful_job: Industrial heat-pump projects are accepted using inconsistent boundaries and steady-state snapshots even though auxiliary loads, variable flow, steam quality, fouling, and transient operation determine actual savings. Integrators need a defensible field acceptance dossier, not another laboratory nameplate test.
selected.product: A portable island of nonintrusive electrical metering, clamp-on ultrasonic flow, calibrated temperature and pressure sensing, steam-enthalpy estimation, synchronized acquisition, uncertainty propagation, and a boundary-defined transient COP/exergy report.
selected.noncosmetic_wedge: Intertek, TÜV SÜD, AHRI programs, and national laboratories provide certification and rig testing. The wedge is rapid on-site whole-boundary transient M&V under actual variable load, including auxiliaries and steam delivery. MIIT's stated need for wide-range actual-load evaluation makes this more than a reporting interface.
selected.precompany_plan_2026_2029: 2026: freeze boundary and uncertainty protocol. 2027: instrument a 300 kW-3 MW partner loop. 2028: complete two seasonal field deployments and obtain third-party sensor calibration. 2029: win one paid commissioning engagement in CN and one US demonstration or ESCO evaluation.
selected.launch_2030_timing_thesis: China's official heat-pump action plan sets 2030 deployment and industrialization objectives, while MIIT's 2026-2028 program explicitly calls for industrial heat pumps and wide-range actual-load efficiency evaluation. The validation window precedes the scale-up and acceptance wave.
selected.demand_trigger_2030_2034: Industrial-steam and waste-heat projects installed under the 2026-2030 action-plan cycle reach acceptance, optimization, and performance-guarantee review. In the US, ongoing DOE high-temperature-heat-pump demonstrations provide a partner route, but the US beachhead is conditional on a paid 2029 field engagement.
selected.competition_outlook_2030: Large test houses can extend into field M&V and heat-pump OEMs can bundle sensors. The candidate wins only if it closes a whole-system energy balance faster and more accurately than ad hoc consultant instrumentation, with a reusable acceptance protocol.
selected.china_route: Use locally sourced instrumentation and domestic calibration laboratories; sell field commissioning to civilian industrial owners, integrators, and energy-service firms. No restricted technology transfer is required.

first_experiment.design: Instrument one partner heat-pump loop between 300 kW and 3 MW, compare against traceable reference calorimetry, and introduce blinded operating changes that create approximately 5% degradation.
success_thresholds: Whole-boundary energy-balance closure <=2% at stable points
Transient COP uncertainty <=3% across the prespecified operating envelope
Detect the blinded 5% degradation with >=90% sensitivity
Installation completed in <2 site days and signed report delivered in <24 hours after data close
kill_thresholds: Fails any field accuracy or degradation-detection threshold
Requires invasive plant modifications beyond standard ports
No paid pilot after two witnessed field trials

G1.rationale: Tongji procures exact heat-pump coupled demonstration/testing service, while NDRC and MIIT independently establish funded deployment and real-load evaluation demand.

G2.rationale: A final peer-reviewed monitoring-framework paper supports the measurement problem; no projected product accuracy is borrowed from it.

G3.rationale: The nine-month $68k field experiment has traceable accuracy, uncertainty, detection, deployment-time, and buyer kill thresholds.

G4.rationale: Named test houses and certification programs occupy adjacent territory. Whole-boundary variable-load field acceptance is distinct but absorbable.

G5.rationale: All observables and uncertainty propagation are established engineering; the differentiator is directly testable in one field installation.

G6.rationale: The CN route uses local instrumentation and calibration for civilian efficiency projects with no structural export block.

G7.rationale: The official 2030 heat-pump action plan and independent MIIT 2026-2028 actual-load evaluation program create a specific validation-then-acceptance sequence extending into 2030-2034.

selected.concept: Qualified diamond transmission-dynode membrane and integration cartridge for hybrid MCP-PMTs used in EIC-class photon detectors
named_buyer_examples: Brookhaven National Laboratory LDRD-26-055 hybrid MCP-PMT project
Brookhaven EIC Detector II instrumentation program if funded
US detector laboratories developing RICH, time-of-flight, and fast-photon systems
selected.painful_job: Large-area MCP-PMTs lose photoelectrons at the first plate's non-pore area and must run high MCP gain to recover single photons, increasing accumulated charge and lifetime risk. Brookhaven's 2026 RFI is unusually exact: it asks outside organizations to supply and process thin diamond films, perform laser or RIE thickness reduction, create negative-electron-affinity surfaces, and measure secondary-electron yield for a hybrid MCP-PMT.
selected.product: A reproducible, serialized transmission-dynode membrane package: thickness-controlled conductive CVD diamond, vacuum-stable negative-electron-affinity termination, guarded mount and electrode geometry, incoming electron-yield map, vacuum bake record, and a tube-integrator acceptance dossier. The startup supplies the difficult membrane/process interface and qualification data, not the MCP, photocathode, Timepix4 ASIC, or complete vacuum tube.
selected.frontier_vision: Insert a thin, radiation-hard electron preamplifier ahead of any microchannel plate so detector builders can trade transmission gain for lower MCP voltage, longer life, and higher effective photon-detection efficiency across collider, neutron, medical, and ultrafast-imaging instruments.
selected.precompany_plan_2026_2029: 2026: reproduce published transmission-yield measurements on commercial CVD diamond coupons and negotiate test access with a US electron-source/vacuum lab. 2027: down-select thickness, doping, front electrode, and NEA treatment on at least 12 membranes. 2028: deliver four serialized dynode cartridges for independent SEY, vacuum-bake, and lifetime testing. 2029: require a paid BNL/US-lab qualification, funded Detector II work package, or signed tube-integrator design-in; a research collaboration without a purchasing path does not count.
selected.launch_2030_timing_thesis: Base ePIC photosensor procurement is too early for a 2030 entrant and is explicitly excluded from the base case. The open socket is the separately named EIC Detector II hybrid-MCP-PMT program, post-installation upgrades, replacement lots, and other US fast-photon programs. BNL is doing enabling LDRD and outside-capability market research in 2026, while the EIC master schedule extends detector integration, installation, commissioning, and operations work through 2035. Four years is enough to qualify a supplied membrane/process module without attempting to design the complete detector tube.
selected.demand_trigger_2030_2034: A funded EIC Detector II or ePIC upgrade/spares package that carries the hybrid MCP-PMT beyond LDRD, plus US detector programs purchasing radiation-tolerant, high-rate photon sensors during EIC commissioning and early operation. The trigger is valid only if at least one program funds external dynode hardware by end-2029.
selected.competition_outlook_2030: Closest competitors are Incom's EIC HRPPD/LAPPD products, Exosens/Photonis Planacon and PhotonPix MCP-PMTs, Hamamatsu MCP-PMTs, and BNL's own tube architecture. Incom is already delivering EIC tiles and Exosens claims collection efficiency approaching 100 percent, so incumbent convergence is real. The non-cosmetic wedge is the qualified upstream diamond transmission-gain membrane/process cartridge, which can reduce the charge multiplication demanded from the MCP and is precisely the capability BNL is seeking externally; it is not a different package around an ordinary MCP.
selected.timing_window_risk: EIC Detector II may never receive construction funding, Exosens or Incom may close the collection-efficiency gap without a dynode, or BNL may internalize the process after the LDRD. Do not count base-ePIC procurement. Kill the commercial thesis at end-2029 unless a US lab or tube maker pays for qualification or writes the cartridge into a funded post-freeze detector plan.
selected.commercial_readiness_kill_date: 2034, with an earlier commercial kill at 2029-12-31 absent paid qualification or a funded design-in
selected.extreme_edge: Target transmission secondary-electron gain of at least 8 at 1-3 keV while preserving timing and vacuum stability, allowing roughly an order-of-magnitude reduction in MCP charge gain for an equal downstream pulse in the validated operating point.
selected.first_experiment: 2027-2028, nine months: procure at least 12 CVD diamond films spanning thickness and doping; laser/RIE thin them; apply two NEA treatments and two electrode schemes; map reflection and transmission electron yield in UHV before and after a 200 C bake and after an accumulated input charge test. Pass only if four membranes independently show transmission yield >=8 at <=3 keV, within-wafer yield coefficient of variation <=15%, dark current <=10 nA at the operating bias, <=10% yield loss after bake, and <=20% loss after the accelerated charge dose. Kill on surface instability in air transfer, destructive charging, timing spread >50 ps attributable to the dynode in a pulsed-electron test, or if two tube integrators say the mount cannot be sealed.
selected.design_in_or_procurement_engagement_path: Respond to a follow-on BNL procurement or partner with a US MCP-PMT integrator in 2028; by 2029 require a paid qualification lot, funded EIC Detector II work package, or signed integration specification.
selected.safety_regulatory_export_path: The product is a passive vacuum component, but operation uses kilovolt bias and UHV processing; use interlocked electron-gun/HV stations, vacuum-material traceability, contamination controls, and buyer radiation-qualification procedures. US civilian DOE science is the base case. Classify the detector component and screen end use before any export; no cross-border route is required.
selected.founder_fit_note: Thin-film process control, electronics test, high-voltage measurement, statistical qualification, and supplier automation use generic EE/CE skills; NEA surface chemistry and vacuum-tube sealing require specialist partners.

G1.rationale: BNL RFI 479547 is an exact external-capability request; separate BNL LDRD and EIC records name the Detector II project and current HRPPD orders.

G2.rationale: Six technical journal works have final publisher/DOI evidence; no preprint carries a load-bearing physics claim.

G3.rationale: The nine-month $94k membrane matrix has numerical yield, uniformity, leakage, bake, dose, timing, and integrator-interface kills.

G4.rationale: Incom, Exosens/Photonis, Hamamatsu, and BNL in-house architecture are named. The upstream transmission-gain membrane is a functional multiplication stage that BNL is explicitly sourcing externally.

G5.rationale: Peer-reviewed diamond transmission and NEA emission measurements establish the mechanism; the experiment tests the unproven repeatability and lifetime.

G6.rationale: HV/UHV safety, materials traceability, radiation qualification, US-only base case, and export/end-use screening are explicit.

G7.rationale: The plan excludes frozen base-ePIC procurement, uses a 2026 external RFI plus FY27 Detector II work, cites the official EIC schedule through 2035, and has a hard end-2029 commercial kill.

selected.distinctness_check: Fresh L13 detector-material subsystem; not detector timing, SRF LLRF/piezo, D-16 Brayton, A-05 NEG coating, D-19, A-02, A-21, or A-22.

rejected.reason: Killed: the buyer collaboration and a global facility already built the exact timing endpoint class.
Held: buyer laboratories own the adaptive control functions and no merchant evaluation interface is evidenced.
Killed: exact purification incumbents and helium-free substitution erase the proposed wedge.
Killed: exact domestic incumbents and no defensible 2028-2035 entry trigger.
Killed: the facility schedule moved beyond the required launch window.
Killed: exact incumbent equipment closes both competition and timing gates.
